meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so I'll be direct: why did my son find out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Now tell me what you have, Hale, because a zero needs more than an apology.

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
A log isn't a hearing, Hale. Procedure 4.1 says you speak with Owen first, and 4.2 says you call me before any mark goes in. So who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it was entered?
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.
Turn the screen, Hale. I'm writing down Act 3, Scene 2 and the line. A misquoted line is a bad quotation, so what else do you have besides that?

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

That's 4.4, Hale, and I want it in writing tonight, with the zero out of the gradebook until then. I still haven't seen the scene you're relying on. Who else is in that room Thursday at 8:15, other than the vice-principal?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You offered a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 with the vice-principal present, the new mark to replace the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require the zero out of the gradebook, the scene and the version history in front of me, and the names of everyone who will be in that room. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback; she accepted nothing yet, but treated your supervised rewrite as the right framework and still wants the zero out of the gradebook, the terms in writing, the scene and version history in front of her, and the names of everyone in the room, which is close to the fair outcome of a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under 4.4.
What moved her: You cited the supervised rewrite correctly, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, which met her fallback demand.
What cost ground: You described the version history and the missing line from Hamlet but never put either in front of her, so she had nothing she could check herself and held her position.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history times late on the night before the essay was due came closest to that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked you to turn the screen, show her the version history and the scene right then, before moving on to the rewrite.
